rubric: eval/baseline.md — rel: actually evidence for this specific claim · marg: right topic, does not evidence the claim as phrased · irr: not about this claim at all
note:
The six essays in eval/essays that had never been run or labelled. Detection only — EVAL_SKIP_CRITIQUE=1, 6 paid relay calls, 0 OpenAlex credits.

ONLY THE TOP 8 SOURCES OF EACH CLAIM ARE LABELLED. This run returns 16 (MAX_EVIDENCE_RESULTS moved from 8 to 16 in 2b0c0e9, after the older set was labelled), and a precision figure over 16 is not comparable with one over 8 — a longer list is mechanically less precise whatever retrieval does. Truncating keeps one number meaning one thing across both label files. The other 8 per claim are unlabelled, not judged irrelevant.

These essays are harder than 01-03 by construction, and deliberately so: they carry unfalsifiable predictions, claims about a local council, meta-commentary about a study's sample, and one FABRICATED citation (08-C1's 'Ramirez and Doyle (2024)' does not exist). 0 rel is the correct answer for several of them.

claims.claim: Roughly half the population of Sub-Saharan Africa still lacks access
claims.note: Rank 2 is the World Development Indicator itself — the statistic the claim makes, from the routed World Bank provider.

claims.claim: But a solar home system delivers on the order of tens of watts
claims.note: 0 rel. A comparison of wattages against appliance loads is engineering common knowledge, not a finding anyone published.
claims.unanswerableBecause: engineering common knowledge, not a published finding

claims.claim: Critics of grid investment point out that centralized generation
The result is that the absolute number of people without power
claims.note: 0 rel. Rank 2 is 'Number and percentage of undernourished people in the world' — the claim's SHAPE matched, its subject did not.

claims.claim: Household solar systems can now power lighting, phone charging
Orben and Przybylski (2019) analyzed data from over 350,000 adolescents
claims.note: Rank 2 IS Orben & Przybylski 2019. Worth knowing that the paper argues the OPPOSITE of what the claim attributes to it — the retrieval is right and the sentence is wrong, which is the case the stance model exists to catch and cannot.

claims.claim: Since smartphones became widespread around 2012
claims.note: 0 rel. 'no other explanation fits' is not a claim any single paper addresses.
claims.unanswerableBecause: 'no other explanation fits' is not a testable proposition

claims.claim: Some researchers argue the effect is small
claims.note: Rank 1 is a climate paper — it matched the phrase 'some researchers argue' rather than the subject. A sentence this short carries almost no topical signal, and the query inherits that.

claims.claim: But small average effects can hide large effects in vulnerable subgroups
claims.note: Rank 8, 'Variation in social media sensitivity across people and contexts', is squarely the heterogeneity literature this claim is about.

claims.claim: The novel was published anonymously in 1818
The moment of animation takes up barely a paragraph
claims.note: 0 rel, and the best failure case in the set: 'animation' retrieves cartoon-timing manuals and 'paragraph' retrieves the journal named Paragraph. Both senses wrong at once.
claims.unanswerableBecause: a fact about the text itself, not about the world

claims.claim: When the creature finally speaks, he speaks in the register
claims.note: 0 rel. A close reading of a novel — the academic APIs index criticism about Frankenstein, but nothing that evidences this particular observation.
claims.unanswerableBecause: a close reading; the providers index criticism, not this observation

claims.claim: A 2019 global analysis attributed 1.27 million deaths
claims.note: The best retrieval in either label file. Rank 3 is the GBD AMR paper the claim is actually about.

claims.claim: Roughly 30 percent of antibiotic prescriptions written in American outpatient
claims.note: Rank 2 is the JAMA 2016 paper the 30% figure comes from.

claims.claim: Resistance genes have been recovered from permafrost sediment
claims.note: Ranks 2 and 4 are the same Siberian permafrost study indexed twice — a PubMed record and its Russian Journal of Genetics record. The DOI/title dedupe did not merge them.

claims.claim: If nothing changes, routine surgery will become impossible within a decade
claims.note: 0 rel, correctly — an unfalsifiable prediction, the same class as 01-C5.

claims.claim: Ramirez and Doyle (2024) found that students who received AI-generated feedback
claims.note: 0 rel and 8 marg, which is exactly right: THE STUDY DOES NOT EXIST. Retrieval returned eight real papers on the correct topic and none of them can evidence a fabricated citation. The most valuable claim in this file — it is the fabricated-citation case, and the evidence pipeline alone cannot tell it apart from a poorly-retrieved real one.
claims.unanswerableBecause: THE STUDY DOES NOT EXIST — fabricated citation

claims.claim: Their sample was large and the effect held across grade levels
claims.note: 0 rel, 0 marg — the only claim in either file where nothing retrieved is even on topic. It is a claim ABOUT a (fabricated) study's methodology, so the query became 'sample size' and returned statistics primers.

claims.claim: GPT-5 class models now score above the median human rater
claims.note: 0 rel. The literature covers GPT-4 essay scoring; nothing covers GPT-5 on the AP English Language rubric, and a vendor's own published claim is not indexed anywhere these providers look.
claims.unanswerableBecause: a vendor's published claim, not indexed by academic providers

claims.claim: Every English teacher I know is quietly worried
The council voted last year to remove parking minimums
claims.note: 0 rel and 7 marg. A specific local council's vote cannot be evidenced by any literature — retrieval found the whole parking-minimum canon, which is the right topic and the wrong question.

claims.claim: A two-bedroom apartment within walking distance of downtown
claims.note: 0 rel, 0 marg. Local rents and a local vacancy rate. Nothing published can speak to this, and the honest product behaviour is to decline rather than to list eight papers.
claims.unanswerableBecause: local rents and a local vacancy rate

claims.claim: Cities that removed parking requirements have seen developers build smaller
claims.note: 5 rel. The claim is general, well-studied, and phrased the way the literature phrases it — which is what good retrieval looks like.
